articles.summary: What happens when structure is treated not as something added to architecture, but as something the architecture itself provides?

articles.title: Sage Guangzhou Aranya Store / say architects
articles.summary: Rooted in Aranya Guangzhou's site DNA—"half urban bustle, half lake-and-mountain scenery"—and meeting Sage Studio's natural, relaxed lifestyle ethos, a new context takes shape. A lived-in sensibility reconciles the everyday with the poetic; directness runs through material and structure; playfulness threads scene and experience. Here, say builds for sage a small house made for holidays.

articles.title: Anja House / iHouse estudio
articles.summary: Casa Anja is a home designed as a holiday retreat for a family, envisioned for the summer months, winter breaks, and weekend getaways. Located in a pine forest in La Barra, Punta del Este , the house proposes a direct relationship with the landscape, treating the existing vegetation not as a constraint but as the starting point for the project.

articles.title: FG House / Oficina Conceito Arquitetura
articles.summary: Located in the southern zone of Porto Alegre, Casa FG was conceived as an urban refuge: a contemporary residence that embraces the site's 16-foot slope as a design concept, making the view of the Guaíba River the central focus. The property, previously occupied by a house that felt more like a country estate, retains a close-knit neighborhood character typical of smaller towns — a rare and valuable quality in an urban context. It was here that the family found the perfect spot for their new home, featuring a spacious social area, bedrooms, a swimming pool, a terrace, and a pool house.

articles.title: Casa Canal / Este Norte Estudio
articles.summary: Yes, you are tucked away in the middle of the woods, and sometimes I think I can't see you from above because the treetops hide you. So I look for your left side, the one touching the river, and there I find you. Sometimes I look at you from the front and I can't believe how you turned out, because we designed you to be fresh and, truth be told, you are. And I'm not sure if that is so easily achieved.

articles.title: House in Santa Maria da Feira / Branco-DelRio Arquitectos
articles.summary: The house is situated on a walled, densely wooded plot, where the presence of mature vegetation defines the character of the site and establishes a sense of interiority and privacy. The property is set on sloping terrain organized around a courtyard, whose spatial structure and relationship with the topography were preserved as the foundation of the project.

articles.title: Indigenous House / Formline Architecture + Urbanism + LGA Architectural Partners
articles.summary: Indigenous House reflects the University of Toronto Scarborough's commitment to renewing and strengthening its relationship with Indigenous communities. Prominently situated at the centre of campus, the project plays a meaningful and visible role in the university's academic and cultural mission to address Canada's Truth and Reconciliation Commission's Calls to Action.

articles.title: MacIsaac Health Building / SHL
articles.summary: The University of British Columbia (UBC) in Vancouver , Canada, ranks among the world's best universities. The new MacIsaac Health Building at the university's Point Grey campus entrance is designed to reflect UBC's reputation as a world-class institution for higher education, as well as its promise to support inclusivity, sustainability, and student well-being.

articles.title: Combining 3D Printing with Weaving
articles.summary: Amsterdam-based Joram de Haas calls himself an industrial and computational designer. His FilaLoom project, done as his Master's thesis in Integrated Product Design at TU Delft, combines 3D printing with textile weaving. He's rigged up a 3D printer that can do both FDM and lay yarn between the printed elements. FilaLoom gives a new capability to FDM-printers, embedding yarns directly onto printed objects, allowing us to explore a novel design space at the intersection of additive manufacturing and textile making. The one on the left is the power button, which lights up to let you know it's on. The knob at the right controls the volume. It also doubles as a button: One press is play/pause, two presses goes to the next track, three presses goes to the previous track. articles.title: Maya Barkai's "Walking Men" Public Art Installations
articles.summary: Since 2009, NYC-based photographer Maya Barkai has been exhibiting Walking Men , a traveling public art project. Barkai gathered images of the striding figure on Walk/Don't Walk signs from cities around the world, and presents them in life-sized displays. The project has popped up in New York, Sydney, Taipei and Perm, Russia. A spin-off installation compiled Men at Work representations, and was shown in Israel and New York. Barkai sells limited edition prints here .
